title: The Lord My Pasture Shall Prepare
description: The Lord My Pasture Shall Prepare in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Joseph Addison wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 495 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God our Shepherd”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord my pas-ture shall pre-pare, And feed me with a shep-herd's care; His pre-sence shall my wants sup-ply, And guard me with a watch-ful eye; My noon-day walks he shall at-tend, And all my mid-night hours de-fend.

lines: The Lord my pasture shall prepare,
And feed me with a shepherd's care;
His presence shall my wants supply,
And guard me with a watchful eye;
My noonday walks he shall attend,
And all my midnight hours defend.
When in the sultry glebe I faint,
Or on the thirsty mountains pant,
To fertile vales and dewy meads
My weary, wandering steps he leads,
Where peaceful rivers, soft and slow,
Amid the verdant landscape flow.
Though in the paths of death I tread,
With gloomy horrors overspread,
My steadfast heart shall fear no ill,
For thou, O Lord, art with me still.
Thy friendly staff shall give me aid,
And guide me through the dreadful shade.
Though, in a bare and rugged way,
Through devious, lonely wilds I stray,
Thy bounty shall my pains beguile, —
The barren wilderness shall smile,
With sudden greens and herbage crowned
And streams shall murmur all around.

licence: Public domain: Joseph Addison died in 1719.
credits: Words by Joseph Addison (1672–1719), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
